entities.summary:
Pope Boniface V was the pivotal figure who shaped the Christianisation of Anglo-Saxon England, leaving a lasting legacy through the sanctuary decree that transformed churches into places of refuge.

Born in 560 AD, Boniface V's papacy was marked by his efforts to secure the support of the Frankish king Sigebert III for the Christian faith.

On December 23, 619, Boniface V was elected as the 105th Pope of Rome, succeeding Pope Boniface IV. His papacy lasted until his death on October 25, 625.

During his tenure, Boniface V issued the decree that churches became places of sanctuary, providing a safe haven for persecuted Christians. This move not only strengthened the Christian community but also facilitated the spread of Christianity throughout Anglo-Saxon England.

The sanctuary decree was a significant turning point in the history of the English church, as it provided a legal and social framework for the protection of Christians. It also marked a shift in the role of the church, as it began to take on a more active role in providing assistance to the poor and vulnerable.

The legacy of Boniface V can be seen in the continued importance of churches as places of refuge and worship. His efforts to promote Christianity in Anglo-Saxon England also paved the way for the conversion of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom to Christianity.

In conclusion, Pope Boniface V played a crucial role in shaping the course of Christian history, particularly in the context of Anglo-Saxon England.
